author: Baron Godfrey Rathbone Benson Charnwood
claims: The Gettysburg Address is described as a little speech.
It is characterized by its singular perfection of form.
It is considered one of the chief outstanding examples of Lincoln's peculiar oratorical power, alongside the 'Second Inaugural'.
